In the first 20 minutes of the match, both sides played with plenty of fire, and after the "water break," players from each team received yellow cards — England's midfielder Elliot Anderson and Argentina's centre-back Lisandro Martínez. By halftime, almost every whistle was met with cheers from fans backing their team and boos at fouls from the opposition.

The sides went into halftime level, but after the second-half switch of ends, in the 55th minute England's Anthony Gordon picked up a pass and fired Argentina's goal open first, taking a 1-0 lead, sparking immediate celebrations among England fans throughout the stadium.

After falling behind, Argentina surged back into the contest. Within 10 minutes they launched three attacks built on crosses from the right, all of which were blocked, drawing sighs from many Argentina supporters. It was not until the 85th minute that Enzo Fernández met a pass from Messi and headed home to draw Argentina level at 1-1, sending Argentina fans into wild celebrations of drumming and horn-blowing.

In added time in the 92nd minute, Messi provided the assist and Lautaro Martínez struck the killer blow against England, sending Argentina through to the final once more to contest the World Cup trophy with Spain. Argentina fans across the stadium went wild again, and as the final whistle blew supporters kept embracing in joyous celebration, with some holding up cardboard cutouts of Messi.

Argentina fan A-ho says he has been a fan of Messi since the Argentine first emerged at Barcelona. Wearing an Argentina "two-star" number 10 shirt, he says this World Cup is Messi's last while also defending the title. With his idol Messi and the team sparking debate throughout the tournament, A-ho believes that rather than arguing over every refereeing decision, fans should cherish Messi's final days representing his country. With a smile, he added that while he is still young enough to take it, he chose to stay up late at a shopping mall to enjoy the occasion with other fans, saying the atmosphere beats watching at home, and in the end the result went the way he had hoped, with Argentina reaching the final.

England fans had been chanting "Football's coming home!" throughout the tournament, but were unable to take football home once more. Declan, who is studying in the UK, returned to Hong Kong for the summer. Today he draped himself in an England flag and, amid the fierce battle between the two sides, cheered on full-throttle with his friends. He said this was his first time watching a match at a shopping mall to soak up the atmosphere, and felt that while the fans were passionate they also respected each other, with no excessive clashes.

When your team loses, disappointment is unavoidable. Declan — who shares a name with England midfielder Declan Rice — felt England had performed creditably in the match. A fan for two tournaments, he said plainly, "We've waited 60 years, waiting another four is no big deal!"

Argentina will face Spain on the 20th bidding to defend the title, while in the third-place playoff England will meet France on the 19th.
